desc:
Ecommerce platform comparison and advice helps you pick where your store should live, or decide whether to stay put. Ecom Swift LLC compares platforms against your products, team and budget, and writes a plain recommendation you can act on.

## What is ecommerce platform advice?

Platform advice is an independent comparison of the software options for running your online store. The usual candidates are Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix and Squarespace. Each has strengths: some are quick to launch, some offer deep control, some suit large catalogs, some suit small design-led shops.

The goal is not a winner in general. It is the best fit for your store, with the costs and limits written down before you commit.

## Why the choice deserves real analysis

Platforms look similar on their homepages. The differences show up later: transaction fees, app costs, product limits, hosting duties, how checkout can be changed and how easy it is to leave. Forum opinions rarely mention your situation, and a recommendation that suited someone selling digital downloads may be wrong for a shop with hundreds of variants.

Moving platforms is also work. Choosing well the first time avoids a second migration a year later.

## How the right platform affects results

The platform affects speed of change, running costs and growth room. A good fit lets you add products, run promotions and change layouts without a developer. A poor fit makes simple tasks slow and pushes you toward paid add-ons to cover basic gaps.

It also affects conversion indirectly. Checkout features, page speed, mobile themes and payment options vary by platform and plan. Those details influence how many visitors finish an order. Costs matter too: a lower monthly fee can be wiped out by app subscriptions or fees on each sale.

## What a good comparison covers

- Your product types, number of variants and sales channels.
- Team skills, such as whether anyone can manage code or hosting.
- Monthly fees, transaction fees and the cost of the apps you would need.
- Payment methods available in your countries.
- Shipping, tax and multi-currency support.
- Design flexibility and the quality of mobile themes.
- Search engine features and URL control.
- Limits that could hit you, such as product counts or checkout customization.
- Ease of leaving, including how well your data can be exported later.
- A clear verdict, including the option of staying where you are.

## What we do

We begin with a short conversation about what you sell, where you sell it and what is going wrong today. We then research the platforms that fit and build a side-by-side comparison with the costs written out for your case.

You receive a written recommendation with reasons. Bigger packages add a yearly fee estimate, a checklist of your must-have features, a multi-year cost model in a sheet and an outline of the migration steps. We explain the trade-offs honestly, including when the best answer is not to move.

We have no reason to favor one platform. If you then choose to move, we can plan and carry out the work, but you are free to take the advice elsewhere.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- List your must-have features before you compare.
- Count app costs as part of the platform price.
- Try a demo or trial before you decide.
- Think about where the store will be in three years.
- Ask what it costs to leave as well as to join.

**Avoid:**
- Choosing on a friend's recommendation alone.
- Judging a platform by its cheapest plan.
- Moving only because a competitor did.
- Ignoring the skills your team really has.
- Treating the move as a technical task only.

## Who this is for

A new seller deciding where to open a first store. An owner unhappy with the current platform who suspects the grass is greener elsewhere. A growing brand that has hit a limit and wants a clear view of the options.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you sell, how many products you have, which countries you ship to and what budget range you have in mind. If you already run a store, share its address and, if you wish, staff or collaborator access so we can see how it is built. We never need passwords.
